introduction: Today we celebrate the Immaculate Conception of the Blessed Virgin Mary. From the first moment of her existence, by a unique grace given in view of the merits of her Son, Mary was preserved from every stain of original sin. In the middle of Advent, she shows us what God's grace can do and how to welcome Christ. As we celebrate, let us thank God for Mary, full of grace, and ask her to pray for us.

prayerOfTheFaithful.invitation: With Mary, whom God prepared to be the Mother of his Son, let us bring our prayers to the Father.
intentions: For the Church: that, like Mary, she may always say yes to God's word and bring Christ to the world. Let us pray to the Lord.
For all mothers, and for those expecting a child: that they may be blessed and protected, and that every child may be welcomed with love. Let us pray to the Lord.
For those trapped in sin or addiction: that through Mary's intercession they may find freedom in Christ. Let us pray to the Lord.
For young people discerning their vocation: that they may listen to God's call with Mary's openness and courage. Let us pray to the Lord.
For our parish: that in this Advent season we may prepare a pure dwelling for the Lord in our hearts. Let us pray to the Lord.
prayerOfTheFaithful.conclusion: God of all grace, you preserved the Virgin Mary from all sin to make her a worthy mother for your Son. Through her prayers, hear our petitions and help us to welcome Christ with pure hearts. Through Christ our Lord.

reflection.title: Full of grace from the beginning
reflection.body:
Today's feast is often misunderstood. The Immaculate Conception is not the conception of Jesus in Mary's womb, which we hear about in the Gospel. It is Mary's own conception in the womb of her mother. In 1854 Pope Pius IX defined as a doctrine of faith that Mary, from the first moment of her conception, was preserved free from all stain of original sin, by a singular grace of God and in view of the merits of Jesus Christ.

The first reading takes us back to the beginning, when sin first entered the world. After Adam and Eve hide from God, he speaks to the serpent: "I will put hostility between you and the woman, and between your offspring and her offspring. He will bruise your head, and you will bruise his heel." Christian tradition has seen in these words a first glimpse of the Gospel: a woman and her child who will overcome evil.

The Church has long seen Mary in that woman. She did not earn her holiness; it was a pure gift, given so that she could be a fitting mother for the Son of God. Mary too was saved by Christ, only in a unique way: not lifted out of sin after falling, but kept from falling into it at all.

The angel's greeting in the Gospel points to the same truth: "Rejoice, you highly favored one!" Behind "highly favored one" stands a single Greek word, meaning one who has been filled with grace. Full of grace, Mary is free to answer God without hesitation: "Behold, the servant of the Lord; let it be done to me according to your word."

Paul reminds us that this is not only Mary's story. God "chose us in him before the foundation of the world, that we would be holy and without defect before him in love." What God did for Mary from the beginning, he wants to do for us through baptism, confession and a lifetime of grace.

In this Advent season, Mary teaches us how to wait for Christ: with a clean heart, an open ear, and a willing yes.
